messages:
Priya (CSM): Nudging — NimblePay onboarding: customers hitting intermittent 429s on browser preflight when they open the app and do a ~10-concurrent preflight burst. Also seeing a handful of 401s after token refresh.
Alex (CSE): Can you paste the root preflight request headers and any rate-limit headers from the response?
Priya (CSM): From their dev:
```
GET /v1/preflight HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci... (ephemeral)
Origin: https://app.nimblepay.com
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0
```
Response had `429` with headers: `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 12` — sometimes `401` immediately after a refresh.
Jules (Eng): Two quick suspects: 1) browser-side preflight fanout (10 tabs / parallel init) -> backend burst window. 2) token refresh race where multiple tabs refresh and a few requests carry expired tokens -> our auth layer returns 401 then client retries causing 429.
Samir (Platform): Also check if their CDN/proxy strips or replays `Authorization` on connection reuse — we've seen proxies that drop auth on re-used keep-alive streams leading to 401 spikes.
Alex (CSE): Priya — can you ask for their ephem TTL and the refresh logic? Also whether they do a single shared refresh endpoint or each tab refreshes independently.
Priya (CSM): They've got ephems at 60s TTL. Each tab runs its own auth refresh; no cross-tab sync.
Jules (Eng): That's fertile ground for a stampede. Suggestions:
- Increase local backoff + jitter on client preflight retry (recommend: base 200ms jittered, max 2s)
- Move preflight to server-side OR use a single shared refresh mechanism (broadcastChannel/sessionStorage) so only one tab hits the token endpoint
- For onboarding bursts, temporarily advise them to use a long-lived server API key for initial bulk setup (server-to-server) while the browser flows warm up
- Enable connection pooling w/ keep-alive but confirm their proxy preserves `Authorization`
Samir (Platform): On our side we can relax the immediate 429 behavior for auth-paths: add a short token-refresh grace window (1–2s) so a nearly-expired token still authenticates while refresh completes. I can open a patch for canary.
Alex (CSE): Also check `x-client-conn` in their logs; if the same TCP conn suddenly loses auth header that's proxy behavior. Ask them to reproduce with `curl -v --http1.1` to see headers over same conn.
Priya (CSM): I'll send repro steps. Quick note: they also use an internal corporate proxy (SmartProxyX) — could be rewriting headers.
Jules (Eng): If proxy is to blame, ask them to test bypassing proxy or whitelist our domain. Meanwhile we can add advisory: 'browser onboarding: keep ephemeral TTL >= 90s for multi-tab apps' — I'll draft wording.
Priya (CSM): Thanks all — I'll coordinate with NimblePay and report back. @Samir can you flag this for a lightweight canary for the grace-window?
Samir (Platform): On it — filing runbook ticket.
OpsBot: ticket #CS-4129 created by Samir: 'preflight auth grace-window canary' :white_check_mark:
Priya (CSM): Closing loop — nimble devs will test server-side kickstart + cross-tab refresh. I'll post results here.
